## Description
&#10;&#9;&#9;1. Reduction to Pig Iron: Iron oxide (ore) is mixed with coke (carbon) and &#10;&#9;&#9;   limestone in a blast furnace heated to approximately 2,000°C. The carbon monoxide generated from &#10;&#9;&#9;   the coke strips oxygen from the iron oxide, reducing it to molten pig iron (containing 3–4% carbon) &#10;&#9;&#9;   and slag, which is tapped off. &#10;&#9;&#9;2. Refining to Steel: The molten pig iron is transferred to a Basic Oxygen Furnace (BOF) &#10;&#9;&#9;   or an Electric Arc Furnace (EAF). In the BOF, pure oxygen is blown into the melt to oxidize &#10;&#9;&#9;   and remove excess carbon (lowering it to 0.1–2%) and impurities like silicon and phosphorus. &#10;&#9;&#9;   The resulting molten steel is then cast into molds or continuous strands to form steel ingots.&#9;   &#9;   &#10;&#9;&#9;
